newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: ABU DHABI ISLAMIC BANK IPO 20 TIMES OVERSUBSCRIBED.
newsitem.headline: ABU DHABI ISLAMIC BANK IPO 20 TIMES OVERSUBSCRIBED.

text.p: Abu Dhabi Islamic Bank's initial public offering was 20 times oversubscribed, newspapers said on Sunday.
They said the bank, which opened for public subscription in late June, received applications totalling 12.4 billion dirhams ($3.38 billion) for shares worth 610 million dirhams.
Some 220,285 people subscribed to the offer.
The bank had offered the public 61 million shares with a par value of 10 dirhams each.

Abu Dhabi, one of the seven emirates of the United Arab Emirates, in May announced the setting up of the bank with a capital of one billion dirhams. Bankers said it would be the biggest Islamic bank in the world.
Islamic banks do not pay interest -- the core of the Western banking system -- because it is regarded by many Moslems as usury, banned under Islamic sharia law.
Papers said the bank's first general assembly would be on September 21.
All subscribers were issued a minimum of 138 shares, they said. ($1=3.67 dirhams)
